title: Shmuel the Elder
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman describes him as a student of R’ Acha, citing [Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 2:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sanhedrin.2.3.8). At the [beginning of chapter 5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sanhedrin.5.1.3), Shmuel the Elder recites a teaching before R’ Acha.
He may be Shmuel Sava, who taught in the name of his son-in-law, Rav Shmuel bar Ami, in [Sotah 10b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.10b.12). Hyman’s printed reference points to 10a.[^3]

notes.text: The complete passage is Sotah 10b, although the notice prints 10a. It reads “Shmuel Sava, father-in-law of Rav Shmuel bar Ami, in the name of Rav Shmuel bar Ami”; the line break and stop in the supplied text must not split the father-in-law’s name. The identification with the Jerusalem Talmud’s Shmuel the Elder remains Hyman’s conjecture.

The saved whole Davidson Sotah10b scalar explicitly has Shmuel Sava, father-in-law of full Rav Shmuel bar Ami, reporting his son-in-law. Supplied line breaks and stops do not split that name into a new chain. Supplied י . conventionally suggests10a despite its spacing; the actual matching10b is shown alongside it, not substituted as printed. Linking this Sava to the JerusalemTalmud student Shmuel the Elder remains Hyman’s possible identification. Sanhedrin2:3/beginning5 were not newly inspected; the abbreviated Acha title stays R', and תני קומי denotes reciting a teaching before him.

Both cited Jerusalem Talmud passages name Shmuel the Elder reciting before Rabbi Acha. Sanhedrin 2:3 concerns the order of voting in capital cases, and 5:1 concerns the seven inquiries. At Sotah 10b the speaker is Shmuel Sava, father-in-law of Rav Shmuel bar Ami, teaching in his son-in-law’s name. The printed Hyman locator has a point after י, which normally points to 10a. The identification of the two Shmuels remains Hyman’s conjecture.
